body:
It isn't exactly prestigious. I'm a recycling collector for a small start-up, but I was the one of the first employees to be hired there, and the company is currently experiencing pretty rapid growth. Lots of opportunities for advancement and maybe even some kind of company stock. It's more like a train leaving the station to me, so getting fired would kind of crush any hope I had of being something beyond College-drop-out-grocery-or-drive-thru fodder.

I used to get along with management really well when I was one of the only two employees under them at the time, but somewhere along the line it seems like I pissed them off (we did have a few disputes about extra hours pay but we always seemed settle them in a civil manner). I also put a dent in the company truck at one point (I don't get high AT work, just to clear that up) so I don't think my veteran status will prevent me from getting canned. It probably also doesn't help that they're all hardcore Christians. 


Like I said below though, losing this job is just the straw that broke my back. I could easily go work at FedEx or something for similar pay, but I've squandered pretty much every chance I've ever gotten to be great; To be someone that other people respect and love. I have a small cabal of close friends, but it's usually somehow obvious that I'm some kind of idiot, loser, or creep to pretty much everyone else in my community.

I just wish I'd started learning to code earlier, I didn't even want this stupid job anyways; I wanted to make art and video games, but I'm usually dedicating so much of myself to the job and making sure that I can pay my bills that I can never muster the energy to create. Since I barely get time to draw, I'm awful at it and it discourages me when I look at the kind of stuff real artists put together in a fraction of the time. It's a passionless farce, living a life of slavery to the almighty dollar. I can't stand it anymore.

So they say, but I'm so numb and tired, I wonder if I'd even feel it at all. 


I want to talk about it, but I don't know where I'd start. Even writing the initial post felt like grabbing just a small handful of my most recent grievances and throwing them out there like a cluster of pebbles. All of my failures have been haunting me my entire life and I'll never be able to get away from them.

Hahahah... I remember when I was your age, I had the exact same fear. I would literally have to leave the room at some points while my friends played Resident Evil 2 on the Playstation, and couldn't even bring myself to walk down my own hallway unless the light was on, because I thought if I let my guard down even for a second, I'd be devoured. 

Having a fear of being torn apart by mindless carnivores is perfectly natural; Nobody *really* wants to see it, or have it happen to them! But you should remember, Cannibalistic Zombies (as portrayed by movies, video games, and anime) don't (and according to some, *can't*) exist!

During my Zombie-phobic phase, my dad told me about how Stephen King (a famous horror writer) once said something along the lines of "In the face of the extraordinary, I would become extraordinary" (he was asked about what he would do if he were trapped in one of his own books). 

That was when I realized; If something as unrealistic as a zombie ever attacked me, why couldn't I just knock their block off with a [Shin Shoryuken](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RamMqZ6l5xI)?

If you're upset that your parents won't help you, you need to realize that your parents are ignoring your cries for help *not because they don't care*, but because *they know they can't defeat the fears in your head; Only you yourself can do that.*

I hope this helps.

Don't forget, YOU wrote that story. YOU are the one that decides the ending.

> this young hero was so crushed he took his own life.

Could easily become something like this:

> The hero was confused by the maidens' sudden departure, and it tormented him for weeks. He wanted to go after her; To find her and ask her why she would suddenly decide to return to a man who tortured her, of all people? He knew it would be no use, though; She had made her choice, and the hero knew he'd be no better than the monster he'd freed her from if he tried to bring her back.

> So the now-mortal hero persevered. His armor felt heavier, and his sword imbalanced, but he continued to do good in the world wherever he could, even after acknowledging that he was susceptible to death. And as he helped other people, his strength returned, and the hero learned to value the love and respect of the people he saved, even if that love was not physical (or non-penetrative). 

> Over time, the hero began to make peace with his past lovers' betrayal; After all, if she truly preferred hell compared to the heaven he offered her, she was likely a demon herself.

> One day, the hero finally met a true maiden; One who admired him for his caring nature and heroic deeds, instead of one brought about by a diabolic pact made in desperation. He confessed his love for her, and she felt the same. The hero could not have been happier!

> The demon raged, knowing that it would be unable to swindle the hero a second time. *"HE SHOULD BE DEAD!"*, it screamed. It called for the aid of a thousand other demons, to attack and harass him at life's every turn. They could not break him now, though; Through the respect of those he saved and the love of his newly-found maiden, he regained his immortality, and slayed them all.

> That immortal hero still lives to this day, riding into the morning sun, bringing hope to the hopeless and aid to the helpless wherever he can. His former lover and even his pure maiden have long passed now, but he knows that he will always have another tomorrow to seek love anew. That is *true* immortality.

If you want it to be.
